title: 2021年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2021年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 The human thirst for knowledge is the driving force behind our successful development as a species. But curiosity can also be dangerous, leading to setbacks or even downfalls. Given curiosity's complexity, scientists have found it hard to define.

P2 While pinning down a definition has proven tricky, the general consensus is it's some means of information gathering. Psychologists also agree curiosity is intrinsically(内在地) motivated.

P3 Curiosity covers such a large set of behaviors that there probably isn't any single "curiosity gene" that makes humans wonder about and explore their environment. That said, curiosity does have a genetic component. Genes and the environment interact in many complex ways to shape individuals and guide their behavior, including their curiosity.

P4 Regardless of their genetic makeup, infants have to learn an incredible amount of information in a short time, and curiosity is one of the tools humans have found to accomplish that gigantic task.

P5 Hundreds of studies show that infants prefer novelty. It's what motivates non-human animals, human infants and probably human adults to explore and seek out new things before growing less interested in them after continued exposure.

P6 In some situations, the stakes are low and failure is a healthy part of growth. For instance, many babies are perfectly proficient crawlers, but they decide to try walking because there's more to see and do when they stand upright. But this milestone comes at a small cost. A study of 12- to 19-month-olds learning how to walk documented that these children fell down a lot. Seventeen times per hour, to be exact. But walking is faster than crawling, so this motivates expert crawlers to transition to walking.

P7 Sometimes, however, testing out a new idea can lead to disaster. For instance, the Inuit people of the Arctic regions have created incredible modes to deal with the challenges of living in northern climates, but what we forget about are the tens of thousands of people that tried and failed to make it in those challenging landscapes.

questions.q: What does the author say about curiosity?
options: It is too complex for non-scientists to understand.
It is the force that pushes human society forward.
It is a unique trait specific to the human race.
It is often the major cause for human failures.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author say about curiosity? 询问作者明确陈述的内容，而非暗含意 思或主旨概括，属于针对原文具体表述的细节题。

【拆句】题干 What does the author say about curiosity? 是简单特殊疑问句，主干 the author say 接 about curiosity 介词短语作状语，无从句、无否定、无比较，结构平铺直叙、无 陷阱。

【定位】The human thirst for knowledge is the driving force behind our successful development as a species. 人类对知识的渴求是我们作为一个物种成功发展背后的驱动力。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文 scientists have found it hard to define 只说科学家觉得它难定义，并未说非科学 家无法理解；too complex for non-scientists to understand 把对象从“科学家”悄悄换 成“非科学家”、把“难定义”夸大为“无法理解”。 B) ✓ 正确 the driving force behind our successful development as a species ↔ the force that pushes human society forward our successful development as a species ↔human society 预判“好奇心推动人类整体发展”与 It is the force that pushes human society forward 在语义上完全重合，是定位句最干净的同义替换。 C) 无中生有 原文从未说好奇心是“人类专有的特征”，P5 反而提到 non-human animals 也会探索新 事物，a unique trait specific to the human race 与原文相反，属无中生有兼与原文 相反。 D) 过度推断 原文 curiosity can also be dangerous, leading to setbacks or even downfalls 用 also 引出次要补充，often the major cause for human failures 把 setbacks/downfalls 升级为 the major cause，并加上频率词 often，过度推断。 人们对好奇心的普遍理解是什么? A) 它激励人们寻求信息。 B) 它注定会改变人类基因。 C) 它给人们带来的好处多于坏处。 D) 它是所有人类行为的基础。

questions.q: What is the general understanding of curiosity?
options: It motivates people to seek information.
It is destined to transform human genes.
It does people more good than harm.
It underlies all human behaviors.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is the general understanding of curiosity? 只问大家的共识内容是什么，属于 客观信息检索类细节题。

【拆句】题干 What is the general understanding of curiosity? 是“What is 主语？”句型，主语 the general understanding of curiosity 是名词词组，of 短语作后置定语限定 understanding，无陷阱。

【定位】While pinning down a definition has proven tricky, the general consensus is it's some means of information gathering. 尽管要给出确切定义被证明很棘手，普遍共识是好奇心是某种信息收集的手段。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 some means of information gathering ↔motivates people to seek information 预判“好奇心是信息收集的手段”与 It motivates people to seek information 在功能上 等价：好奇心驱动人去寻找/收集信息。 B) 无中生有 原文 curiosity does have a genetic component 只说好奇心有遗传成分，并未说好奇 心“注定要改变人类基因”；destined to transform human genes 不仅方向反转，还把 名词性的“遗传成分”改成动词性的“改造基因”，完全无据。 C) 无中生有 原文 can also be dangerous 与 But curiosity often comes with a cost 都明示了好奇 心的代价，并未给出 “好处大于坏处” 的比较结论；does people more good than harm 凭空加上比较结构。 D) 以偏概全 原文 some means of information gathering 只说好奇心是信息收集的“某种”手段， underlies all human behaviors 把范围夸大到“支配全部人类行为”，远超原文范围。 关于基因如何塑造人们的行为,我们了解到什么? A) 它们决定人们的思维方式。 B) 它们解释了学习中的年龄差异。 C) 它们使人们能够承担重大任务。 D) 它们与环境共同起作用。

questions.q: What do we learn about how genes shape people's behavior?
options: They determine people's way of thinking.
They account for age differences in learning.
They enable people to undertake massive tasks.
They work in conjunction with the environment.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do we learn about how genes shape people's behavior? 问的是文中明示的 机理而非推断，属细节题。 53. What do we learn about how genes shape people's behavior? A) They determine people's way of thinking. B) They account for age differences in learning. C) They enable people to undertake massive tasks. D) They work in conjunction with the environment.

【拆句】题干 What do we learn about how genes shape people's behavior? 主干是 What do we learn about，about 后跟 how 引导的宾语从句 how genes shape people's behavior ——how 在此是“以何种方式”，不是“是否”，提问点落在“机理”而不是“结果存在与否”。

【定位】Genes and the environment interact in many complex ways to shape individuals and guide their behavior, including their curiosity. 基因和环境以许多复杂的方式相互作用，塑造个体并指导他们的行为，包括他们的好奇心。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文谈的是 behavior（行为），选项 way of thinking 偷换为思维方式；且 determine 的力度比 shape and guide 强，原文也强调“与环境互动”，并非基因单方“决定”。 B) 无中生有 原文没有讨论学习中的年龄差异，age differences in learning 完全是凭空添加的 话题。 C) 张冠李戴 原文 infants have to learn an incredible amount of information in a short time 描 述的是婴儿任务量大，并未说基因让人“承担巨大任务”；enable people to undertake massive tasks 把对象张冠李戴。 D) ✓ 正确 Genes and the environment interact in many complex ways ↔ They work in conjunction with the environment shape individuals and guide their behavior ↔work 预判“基因与环境共同起作用”与 They work in conjunction with the environment 在 主语、对象、动作方向上一一对应。 大量研究表明婴儿有什么特点? A) 他们比成年人好奇心强得多。 B) 他们更喜欢追逐所有新奇的事物。 C) 他们的兴趣与成年人不同。 D) 他们表现出非人类动物的行为。

questions.q: What do numerous studies show about infants?
options: They are far more curious than adults.
They prefer to go after all that is novel.
They have different interests than adults.
They show non-human animal behaviors.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do numerous studies show about infants? 问研究“表明了什么”，是对原文研 究结论的直接询问，属细节题。

【拆句】题干 What do numerous studies show about infants? 是“What do A show about B?” 句型，主语 numerous studies、宾语为 What、关于 infants，提问点是“关于婴儿的研究 结论”，无陷阱。 54. What do numerous studies show about infants? A) They are far more curious than adults. B) They prefer to go after all that is novel. C) They have different interests than adults. D) They show non-human animal behaviors.

【定位】Hundreds of studies show that infants prefer novelty. 数以百计的研究表明，婴儿偏爱新奇事物。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文没有对婴儿与成人做“好奇程度比较”，只在末尾说 probably human adults 也会探 索；far more curious than adults 凭空加上比较级 + 程度副词 far more。 B) ✓ 正确 infants prefer novelty ↔They prefer to go after all that is novel 预判“婴儿偏爱新奇事物”与 They prefer to go after all that is novel 几乎逐字对应，是 定位句最干净的同义替换。 C) 偷换概念 原文只说婴儿偏好新奇事物，并没有比较婴儿与成人的兴趣范围；different interests than adults 偷换为“兴趣点的差异”，与原文研究结论不在一个维度。 D) 偷换概念 原文 non-human animals, human infants and probably human adults 把动物、婴 儿、成人并列为同样会“偏好新奇”的群体，并非说婴儿“表现出非人类动物的行为”； show non-human animal behaviors 把并列关系曲解为附属关系。 北极地区因纽特人的例子说明了什么? A) 人类探索好奇心的代价。 B) 寒冷天气令人难以置信的严酷。 C) 源于好奇心的创新想法。 D) 从过去失败中学习的重要性。

questions.q: What does the example of the Inuit people of the Arctic regions illustrate?
options: The cost of humans' curiosity to explore.
The incredible harshness of cold weather.
The innovative ideas stemming from curiosity.
The importance of learning from past failures.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the example of the Inuit people of the Arctic regions illustrate? 明确 把 the Inuit people 标记为 the example，问其“说明了什么”，是典型的例证目的题。

【拆句】题干 What does the example of the Inuit people of the Arctic regions illustrate? 主干 the example illustrate，其中 of the Inuit people of the Arctic regions 嵌套两层 of 短语 作 example 的后置定语；考生易把宾语错认为“因纽特人本身”，实际宾语是 What，即“这 个例子说明了什么”。

【定位】But curiosity often comes with a cost. 但好奇心往往是有代价的。 55. What does the example of the Inuit people of the Arctic regions illustrate? A) The cost of humans' curiosity to explore. B) The incredible harshness of cold weather. C) The innovative ideas stemming from curiosity. D) The importance of learning from past failures.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 But curiosity often comes with a cost ↔The cost of humans' curiosity to explore tens of thousands of people that tried and failed ↔to explore 预判“好奇心要付出代价”与 The cost of humans' curiosity to explore 在“代价 + 好奇 心 + 探索”三要素上完全对应。 B) 答非所问 The incredible harshness of cold weather 只是 living in northern climates 的背景 描述，是例子里的细节，而非例子要支撑的论点；例证目的题不能选例子内部的表层 细节。 C) 以偏概全 原文 created incredible modes to deal with the challenges 与 tens of thousands of people that tried and failed 是一组对比，选项 innovative ideas stemming from curiosity 只看到前者“创新成果”，忽略后者“代价”——而后者才是本段真正想强调的部 分（由 but what we forget about 引出）。 D) 偷换概念 原文 But curiosity often comes with a cost 与 tens of thousands of people that tried and failed 只强调“代价/牺牲”这一客观事实，没有谈“从过往失败中学习”的主观行 动；learning from past failures 把客观代价偷换为主观学习行为。
